what.text: Thymalin is a mix of peptides extracted from the thymus glands of calves, with molecular weights up to 10 kDa. Its developers describe it as an immune-modulating drug. Authors of a 2021 paper write that the Russian Ministry of Health has approved it for medical use since 1982, under registration certificate 82/1108/8, made by Samson-Med in St. Petersburg.

what.text: Thymalin is an animal-tissue extract, not a single defined molecule, and nearly all studies come from one research group.

research.text: Human evidence comes almost entirely from Russian and Ukrainian studies, most published in Russian, with few details in English. No trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. The best-described study is a small open-label trial in COVID-19.

research.title: Thymalin added to COVID-19 treatment

facts.v: Khavinson VK, et al. Stem Cell Rev Rep 2021;17(1):285-90
single-center, open-label, randomized by envelope, against standard care only
92 hospital patients with moderate or severe COVID-19 and low lymphocytes (42 thymalin, 50 control); mean age about 60
thymalin 10 mg into muscle once a day for 5 days, plus standard care
10 to 14 days of treatment, April to July 2020
immune cells, IL-6, C-reactive protein, D-dimer, lung scans

research.found: Inflammation and clotting markers fell faster with thymalin, the authors report. No one died in either group. Lung scans showed progression in 5 control patients and 2 thymalin patients. The paper does not report side effects.

research.title: Thymalin and epithalamin in older people

facts.v: Khavinson VKh, Morozov VG. Neuro Endocrinol Lett 2003;24(3-4):233-40
PubMed lists it as a randomized controlled trial; the abstract does not describe randomization or blinding
6 to 8 years of follow-up; treatment in the first 2 to 3 years

research.found: The authors report 2.0- to 2.1-fold lower death rates on thymalin than in controls, and 4.1-fold lower in a group given thymalin and epithalamin every year for 6 years. The abstract gives no group sizes, doses or numbers of deaths.

research.text: These studies come mainly from one group, were small or poorly described, and have not been repeated by independent researchers in published trials.

us.text: Not FDA-approved for any use. No thymalin product appears in FDA’s drug approval database. Products labelled “research use only” are not for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

after.text: Thymalin is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 bans any pharmacological substance not covered elsewhere with no current approval by any government health regulator for human use. Whether thymalin falls under S0 depends on its approval status, which the lists do not address.

unconfirmed: Thymalin’s registration in Russia comes from the study authors (approved since 1982, certificate 82/1108/8); the Russian state drug register (GRLS) showed a CAPTCHA and could not be opened.
UK (MHRA) status and Australia’s TGA register were not checked against the regulator’s own record.
Most thymalin papers are in Russian; only English abstracts were read, except for the 2021 COVID-19 paper.
surprises: Thymalin is promoted for longevity on the basis of a 2003 report of halved death rates, but the abstract gives no group sizes, doses or deaths, and no independent trial has repeated it.
It is sold online as a thymus “peptide”, but it is an extract from calf thymus, not a single defined peptide.
